title: Counterexamples for BFGS-type methods under arbitrary strong Wolfe constants
summary: Whether the Broyden-Fletcher-Goldfarb-Shanno (BFGS) method and its variants can fail to converge on smooth nonconvex functions under realistic line-search parameters has remained a central open problem in quasi-Newton theory since the landmark counterexample of Dai (2002), which was confined to small Armijo parameters ($c_1 \le 1/84 \approx 0.0119$ on Powell's geometry, or $c_1 \le 69/7480 \approx 0.0092$ on his six-point cycle) and an objective function unbounded below. In this paper, we resolve the long-standing open question, posed by Dai (2002) following a discussion with J. C. Gilbert,…
